nodes.summary: If $f$ is a morphism from a DFA $M$ to a DFA $N$ over the same alphabet, then $M$ and $N$ accept the same language.
nodes.title: DFA morphisms preserve the accepted language

nodes.summary: For an accessible DFA $M$, the canonical residual map from $M$ to the residual-language DFA of its accepted language is injective if and only if $M$ is state-separated, that is, any two states of $M$ with the same continuation language are equal.
nodes.title: Injectivity of the canonical residual map

nodes.summary: For an accessible DFA $M$, every state of the residual-language DFA of the language accepted by $M$ is the image of some state of $M$ under the canonical residual map.
nodes.title: The canonical residual map is surjective

nodes.summary: For an accessible DFA $M$ accepting the language $L$, every DFA morphism from $M$ to the residual-language DFA of $L$ equals the canonical residual map.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the canonical residual map

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an accessible DFA accepting the language $L$. The residual-language DFA of $L$ has as states the left quotients $x^{-1}L = \{y \mid xy \in L\}$ for words $x$, start state $L$, transitions $K \mapsto a^{-1}K$ on a symbol $a$, and a state $K$ is accepting when it contains the empty word. The canonical residual map is the DFA morphism from $M$ to this DFA that sends each state $q$ of $M$ to its continuation…
nodes.title: The canonical residual map

nodes.summary: If $f$ is a DFA morphism from $M$ to $N$ and $g$ is a DFA morphism from $N$ to $P$, where $M$, $N$, $P$ are DFAs over the same alphabet, then the composite of $g$ and $f$ is the DFA morphism from $M$ to $P$ whose state map is $g \circ f$.
nodes.title: Composition of DFA morphisms

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be DFAs over the same alphabet with transition functions $\delta_M$ and $\delta_N$. A morphism from $M$ to $N$ is a map $f$ from the states of $M$ to the states of $N$ that sends the start state of $M$ to the start state of $N$, satisfies $f(\delta_M(q, a)) = \delta_N(f(q), a)$ for every state $q$ of $M$ and every symbol $a$, and such that each state $q$ of $M$ is accepting if and only if $f(q)$ is…
nodes.title: Morphisms of DFAs

nodes.summary: For every deterministic automaton $M$ on finite words, the DFA with the same states, transition function, start state and accepting states as $M$ accepts exactly the language of $M$.
nodes.title: Converting a CSLib automaton to a Mathlib DFA preserves its language

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA, write $\delta^*(q, x)$ for the state $M$ reaches from the state $q$ by reading the word $x$, and let $L_M(q)$ be the language of words accepted by $M$ when started in $q$. For every state $q$ and every word $x$, the left quotient $\{z : xz \in L_M(q)\}$ of $L_M(q)$ by $x$ equals $L_M(\delta^*(q, x))$.
nodes.title: Left quotients of continuation languages

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$. The set of left quotients $\{z : xz \in L\}$ of $L$ by words $x$ equals the set of reachable residuals of $M$ (the languages accepted by $M$ from the states it reaches from its start state). The bijection from the first set to the second sends each language to itself.
nodes.title: Left quotients as reachable residuals

nodes.summary: If $f$ is a morphism from a DFA $M$ to a DFA $N$, then for every state $q$ of $M$ and every word $x$, running $N$ on $x$ from $f(q)$ ends in the image under $f$ of the state reached by running $M$ on $x$ from $q$.
nodes.title: DFA morphisms commute with evaluation from a state

nodes.summary: If $f$ is a morphism from a DFA $M$ to a DFA $N$, then for every word $x$, the state that $N$ reaches on input $x$ from its start state is the image under $f$ of the state that $M$ reaches on input $x$ from its start state.
nodes.title: DFA morphisms commute with evaluation

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$, the minimized DFA of $M$ accepts exactly the language accepted by $M$.
nodes.title: The minimized DFA accepts the same language

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$, every state of the minimized DFA of $M$ is reached from its start state by reading some word.
nodes.title: The minimized DFA is accessible

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$. If the set of reachable residuals of $M$ (the states of the minimized DFA of $M$) and the set of Nerode classes of $L$ are both finite, then they have the same number of elements.
nodes.title: When finite, the minimized DFA has as many states as there are Nerode classes

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$, and consider the automaton whose states are the left quotients of $L$, with start state $L$, moving from $K$ on a letter $a$ to $\{z : az \in K\}$. For every word $x$, the state that the minimized DFA of $M$ reaches on $x$, carried to the left quotients of $L$ by the bijection that sends each language to itself, is the state that this automaton reaches on $x$.
nodes.title: Evaluation in the minimized DFA agrees with the left-quotient automaton

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$ and every word $x$, the state that the minimized DFA of $M$ reaches on $x$ is the language accepted by $M$ from the state that $M$ reaches on $x$.
nodes.title: States reached in the minimized DFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA, and for a word $x$ let $[x]$ be the language accepted by $M$ from the state that $M$ reaches on $x$. For every word $x$ and every letter $a$, the minimized DFA of $M$ moves from the state $[x]$ on input $a$ to the state $[xa]$.
nodes.title: Transitions of the minimized DFA on reached states

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA. For every reachable residual $K$ of $M$ (a state of the minimized DFA of $M$) and every letter $a$, the minimized DFA of $M$ moves from $K$ on input $a$ to the left quotient $\{z : az \in K\}$ of $K$ by $a$.
nodes.title: Transitions of the minimized DFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$. The minimized DFA of $M$ has as states the reachable residuals of $M$, that is, the languages accepted by $M$ from the states it reaches from its start state. Its start state is $L$; on a letter $a$ it moves from a state $K$ to the left quotient $\{z : az \in K\}$; and its accepting states are those that contain the empty word.
nodes.title: Minimized DFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA accepting the language $L$. The reachable residuals of the minimized DFA of $M$ and the reachable residuals of $M$ both form the set of left quotients $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ of $L$ by words $x$, and this is the bijection from the first set to the second that sends each language to itself.
nodes.title: Reachable residuals of the minimized DFA

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ and a word $x$, the minimized state of $x$ is the language accepted by $M$ starting from the state that $M$ reaches on reading $x$ from its start state, viewed as an element of the reachable residuals of $M$.
nodes.title: Residual reached by a word

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ accepting the language $L$, there is a bijection from the Nerode classes of $L$ to the reachable residuals of $M$; it sends the class of a word $x$ to the left quotient $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes and reachable residuals

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$ and let $x, y \in \Sigma^*$. Then $x$ and $y$ are related by the Nerode congruence of $L$, that is, $xz \in L \iff yz \in L$ for every word $z$, if and only if they are Nerode equivalent for $L$, that is, their left quotients $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ and $y^{-1}L$ are equal.
nodes.title: The Nerode congruence relates words with equal left quotients

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$, and write $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ for the left quotient of $L$ by a word $x$. This is the bijection from the classes of the Nerode congruence of $L$ onto the set $\{x^{-1}L : x \in \Sigma^*\}$ of residual languages of $L$ that sends the class of each word $x$ to $x^{-1}L$.
nodes.title: Nerode classes are the residual languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$, and write $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ for the left quotient of $L$ by a word $x$. This is the map from the classes of the Nerode congruence of $L$ to the set $\{w^{-1}L : w \in \Sigma^*\}$ of residual languages of $L$ that sends the class of each word $x$ to $x^{-1}L$; it is well defined because Nerode-congruent words have the same left quotient.
nodes.title: The residual language of a Nerode class

nodes.summary: A Mathlib DFA $M$ is viewed as a CSLib deterministic automaton on finite words with the same states, the same transition function, the same start state and the same set of accepting states as $M$.
nodes.title: Mathlib DFAs as CSLib automata

nodes.summary: For every DFA $M$, the identity map on the states of $M$ is a DFA morphism from $M$ to itself.
nodes.title: Identity DFA morphism

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over an alphabet $\Sigma$ accepting the language $L$, and write $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ for the left quotient of $L$ by a word $x$. Consider the canonical automaton of $L$ as a DFA: its states are the classes $[x]$ of the Nerode congruence of $L$, its start state is the class of the empty word, on a letter $a$ it goes from $[x]$ to $[xa]$, and its accepting states are the classes of words of…
nodes.title: The canonical automaton of a DFA's language is its minimized DFA

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $\Sigma$, and write $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ for the left quotient of $L$ by a word $x$. Consider the canonical automaton of $L$ as a DFA: its states are the classes $[x]$ of the Nerode congruence of $L$, its start state is the class of the empty word, on a letter $a$ it goes from $[x]$ to $[xa]$, and its accepting states are the classes of words of $L$. Renaming each…
nodes.title: The Nerode automaton is the residual-language automaton

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA that is accessible and state-separated, and let $L$ be the language it accepts. The map sending each state $q$ of $M$ to the language of words accepted by $M$ starting from $q$ is a bijection from the states of $M$ onto the set of left quotients $\{z : xz \in L\}$ of $L$ by words $x$.
nodes.title: States of an accessible, state-separated DFA correspond to residuals

nodes.summary: A DFA $M$ is state-separated when any two equivalent states of $M$ are equal: if $p \ne q$, then the languages of words accepted by $M$ starting from $p$ and from $q$ are different.
nodes.title: State-separated DFA

nodes.summary: For every language $L$, the residual-language DFA of $L$ is accessible. This automaton has as states the left quotients $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$ for words $x$, start state $L$, transition from $K$ on a letter $a$ to $a^{-1}K$, and accepts $K$ when $K$ contains the empty word.
nodes.title: The residual-language DFA is accessible

nodes.summary: For every language $L$ and every word $x$, the state that the residual-language DFA of $L$ reaches on reading $x$ is the left quotient $x^{-1}L = \{z : xz \in L\}$. This automaton has the left quotients of $L$ as states, start state $L$, transition from $K$ on a letter $a$ to $a^{-1}K$, and accepts $K$ when $K$ contains the empty word.
nodes.title: States reached in the residual-language DFA

nodes.summary: A CSLib deterministic automaton $M$ on finite words is viewed as a Mathlib DFA with the same states, the same transition function, the same start state and the same set of accepting states as $M$.
nodes.title: CSLib automata as Mathlib DFAs
Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
